_comment: Ground truth for the simulated enterprise systems. This is the world the
tools observe -- it is NOT the workflow's answer key. The graph never reads
this file: it has to reach the root cause through search_logs /
get_service_metrics / get_recent_changes / search_knowledge_base like a real
engineer would. Handout ground rule 16 bans hard-coding the visible answers
into the workflow; giving the mock systems a consistent internal state is
what makes the simulation honest rather than what makes it cheat.
To add the hidden scenario: append one entry under 'services'. No code change.

knowledge_base.title: Database connection pool exhaustion
symptoms: request timed out waiting for connection
error rate spike with normal CPU
knowledge_base.probable_cause: All pooled connections are checked out and callers queue until they time out. Usually follows a traffic increase or a code path that holds connections longer than before.
knowledge_base.content: Raise the pool ceiling first, then restart so the new ceiling is picked up. A restart on its own frees the pool for roughly a minute before it saturates again.

knowledge_base.title: Token validation failures after signing key rotation
symptoms: token rejected unable to verify signature
login failures with normal identity provider latency
knowledge_base.probable_cause: A key rotation retired a signing key that is still present in tokens issued before the rotation, so the validator can no longer resolve the kid.
knowledge_base.content: Roll the JWKS configuration back so the retired key is served again until every in-flight token has expired. Restarting the service does not restore a key that was removed from the key set.

knowledge_base.title: Cache eviction storm driving database load
symptoms: response time increased with normal cpu
knowledge_base.probable_cause: Mass eviction pushes read traffic that the cache normally absorbs onto the database, so query latency and response time climb while application CPU stays flat.
knowledge_base.content: Flush and rebuild the cache so the keyspace repopulates cleanly. Look at deployment history first -- if a change shortened the TTL, a flush only helps until the next expiry wave.

knowledge_base.title: Service restart runbook
knowledge_base.probable_cause: Process-level state that cannot be cleared while the service is running.
knowledge_base.content: A rolling restart drops in-flight requests. Treated as a high-risk action: it needs an approver before execution.

knowledge_base.title: Rolling back a configuration or deployment change
symptoms: incident started shortly after a change
knowledge_base.probable_cause: A recent change introduced the fault.
knowledge_base.content: Correlate the incident start with the change feed before rolling back. Rollback is high risk: it reverts everything else in the same change.

knowledge_base.title: Infrastructure saturation
knowledge_base.probable_cause: The host or container is out of headroom.
knowledge_base.content: Confirm CPU and memory are genuinely saturated before scaling. Normal CPU during a latency incident points somewhere else.

incident_history.summary: Payment error rate rose to 12% with database connection timeouts.
incident_history.root_cause: Connection pool exhausted after a traffic increase.
incident_history.resolution_action: Pool size raised from 20 to 50, followed by a restart to apply it.

incident_history.summary: Intermittent authorisation failures from the upstream provider.
incident_history.resolution_action: Waited for the provider; no local action taken.

incident_history.summary: Widespread login failures; tokens rejected at validation.
incident_history.root_cause: Expired signing certificate was still referenced by the JWKS endpoint.
incident_history.resolution_action: Configuration rolled back, then the certificate was replaced during a maintenance window.

incident_history.root_cause: Redis eviction storm left the cache cold; reads fell through to the database.
